rendered: The question's premise does not hold. NFA-F did not show the best capacity retention; it showed the weakest of the variants. Fig. 8[1] shows the NFA-F curve ending lowest. The text names the NFA-A variant as the best, at ≈80%[2] after 100 charge/discharge cycles[3], against ≈70%[4] for NFA 811[5] and ≈50%[6] for NFA-F. The document does not test why NFA-F fades fastest. It offers only a hypothesis: the authors write that we hypothesize that, increasing the iron[7] content from 5% to 15% in these materials may result in[8] mental structural transitions that can cause capacity fade upon[9] continuous charge/discharge cycling. The authors present this as a hypothesis and say the iron redox process and its effect on performance are still being investigated.
